goi-ca-nam-o-da-nang.name: Nam O Fish Salad, Da Nang
goi-ca-nam-o-da-nang.serving_basis: Four portions of dry-style herring salad wrapped with edible wild greens and rice paper, served with cooked Nam O dipping sauce.
goi-ca-nam-o-da-nang.description: A specialty of the Nam O fishing village, made with thin herring fillets mixed with toasted rice powder, galangal, ginger and sesame. Wrap with edible wild greens and rice paper, then dip in a thick Nam O fish sauce.
goi-ca-nam-o-da-nang.finished_dish: Chilled herring is nutty and fragrant with toasted rice powder, galangal, ginger and sesame. Edible wild greens balance the fish; cooked Nam O dipping sauce is savory, lightly sweet and spicy.
goi-ca-nam-o-da-nang.serving: Serve the fish and dipping sauce separately with edible greens and rice paper. Wrap each bite as you eat and serve promptly while the fish is cold.
goi-ca-nam-o-da-nang.image_alt: Dry-style Nam O fish salad with herring coated in toasted rice powder, edible wild greens, rice paper and Nam O dipping sauce.
goi-ca-nam-o-da-nang.time_note: Editorial estimate; actual time depends on fish preparation and available greens.
goi-ca-nam-o-da-nang.recipe_family: Nam O Fish Salad, Da Nang
search_terms: Nam O fish salad, Da Nang
dry herring salad with toasted rice powder
rice paper and edible wild greens
tips: This is a raw-fish dish. Use fish from a trusted supplier who confirms it is suitable for raw consumption; keep chilled, use separate utensils and serve promptly.
Lime or vinegar adds the traditional tart flavor; it is not a safety treatment for raw fish.
If the fish source and handling cannot be confirmed, do not serve this raw version; cooked fish would be a different variation.

ingredients.name: Fresh herring fillets
ingredients.notes: Use fish from a trusted source that confirms it is suitable for raw consumption; keep chilled and use dedicated utensils.

ingredients.name: Toasted rice powder
ingredients.notes: Use some to coat the fish and the rest to season the dipping sauce.

ingredients.name: Edible wild greens
ingredients.notes: Use positively identified edible leaves or common raw-eating herbs.

ingredients.name: Toasted rice crackers
ingredients.notes: Break into pieces for a crisp accompaniment.

ingredients.name: Lime juice
ingredients.notes: Adds tart flavor; the finished dish remains raw fish.

ingredients.name: Galangal
ingredients.notes: Finely chop and divide between fish and sauce.

ingredients.name: Roasted peanuts
ingredients.notes: Crush and divide between fish and sauce.

ingredients.name: Nam O fish sauce or first-press fish sauce
ingredients.notes: Base for the cooked dipping sauce.

ingredients.name: Salt
ingredients.notes: For rinsing fish; omit if the supplier has prepared it.

preparation_steps: Keep fish chilled until preparation. Use a clean knife, board and bowl reserved for raw fish; check for bones, slice thinly and refrigerate.
Rinse greens under clean running water and drain well. Chop galangal, ginger, garlic and chili; crush peanuts and prepare rice paper.
Mix fish sauce with water, galangal, ginger, garlic, chili and sugar. Bring to a full boil, reduce the heat and stir in toasted rice powder gradually until thick; season and cool.
cooking_steps: Place fish in a chilled bowl and add enough lime juice for the salad's tart flavor. Keep briefly refrigerated and drain. Lime does not replace the need to choose fish suitable for raw consumption.
Mix fish with galangal, ginger, toasted rice powder, sesame and some peanuts. Keep chilled until just before serving.
Arrange fish, greens, rice paper, rice crackers and sauce separately. Wrap each bite as eaten, dip and serve immediately; do not leave raw fish at room temperature.

keywords: Nam O Fish Salad, Da Nang

banh-uot-long-ga-da-lat.name: Da Lat steamed rice sheets with chicken and offal
aliases: Lam Dong chicken intestine wet cake
banh-uot-long-ga-da-lat.serving_basis: Four bowls of warm steamed rice sheets with shredded chicken, chicken offal and fresh herbs.
banh-uot-long-ga-da-lat.description: Hot, soft wet cake served with shredded boiled chicken, cooked chicken intestines, laksa leaves and sweet and sour fish sauce - a familiar breakfast dish of Da Lat.
banh-uot-long-ga-da-lat.finished_dish: A bowl of soft steamed rice sheets with sweet shredded chicken, tender chicken offal, fragrant Vietnamese coriander and sweet-sour fish sauce.
banh-uot-long-ga-da-lat.serving: Gently toss the rice sheets, chicken, offal and herbs with the fish sauce just before serving so the sheets do not turn soggy. A small bowl of hot chicken broth is optional.
banh-uot-long-ga-da-lat.image_alt: Da Lat steamed rice sheets with shredded chicken, chicken offal, Vietnamese coriander and cucumber in a blue-and-white ceramic bowl.
banh-uot-long-ga-da-lat.time_note: Estimated editorial timing; actual time depends on equipment, ingredients, and cooking experience.
tips: Simmer the chicken over medium heat and remove it as soon as it is cooked so the meat stays moist.
Cook the chicken offal separately and make sure it is fully cooked before slicing.
Blanch the rice sheets just before serving to keep them soft and warm.
preparation_steps: Rinse the chicken. Rub the offal with salt and rinse it several times; cut the heart, liver and gizzard into bite-sized pieces. Bruise the ginger.
Rinse the Vietnamese coriander, bean sprouts and cucumber; slice the cucumber and onion. Mince the garlic and chili. Mix the fish sauce with sugar, lime juice, garlic, chili and a little warm water.
cooking_steps: Bring water to a simmer with the ginger and some of the salt. Cook the chicken until just done, remove it and let it cool slightly before shredding. Reserve some of the broth for serving if desired.
Cook the chicken offal separately until fully cooked but still tender. Drain and slice.

Briefly blanch the rice sheets and bean sprouts and divide them among bowls. Top with the shredded chicken, offal, cucumber, onion and Vietnamese coriander. Spoon over a little sweet-sour fish sauce and serve while warm.

keywords: Da Lat steamed rice sheets with chicken and offal
Lam Dong chicken intestine wet cake

nem-nuong-ninh-hoa.name: Ninh Hoa grilled pork rolls
aliases: Ninh Hoa grilled spring rolls rolled with rice paper
nem-nuong-ninh-hoa.serving_basis: Four portions of grilled pork to wrap in rice paper with fresh herbs and peanut-soy sauce.
nem-nuong-ninh-hoa.description: Sticky pork rolls, grilled until golden and fragrant, rolled with raw vegetables, bananas, star fruit and pickles; Add flavor with a cup of rich soy sauce.
nem-nuong-ninh-hoa.finished_dish: Ninh Hoa pork rolls are fragrant and golden outside, tender inside, balanced by fresh herbs, pickles and a thick peanut-soy dip.
nem-nuong-ninh-hoa.serving: Serve the pork while hot. Layer it with herbs, green banana, starfruit and pickles on soft rice paper, roll and dip in the sauce.
nem-nuong-ninh-hoa.image_alt: Ninh Hoa grilled pork with rice paper, fresh herbs, green banana, starfruit and a bowl of peanut-soy dipping sauce.
nem-nuong-ninh-hoa.time_note: Estimated editorial timing; actual time depends on equipment, ingredients, and cooking experience.
tips: Knead the pork until tacky so it holds its shape and stays juicy.
Grill over medium heat, turning evenly until golden outside and fully cooked inside.
Season the soybean sauce gradually because saltiness varies by brand.
preparation_steps: Finely dice the pork fat. Mix it with the ground pork, fish sauce, sugar, pepper and some of the minced garlic; knead until tacky.
Rinse the herbs, cucumber, starfruit and green banana; cut them into wrap-sized pieces. Slice the liver and mince the shallots and remaining garlic. Soak the banana in lime water to limit browning.
cooking_steps: Shape the pork into small logs around soaked bamboo skewers or into flat patties. Grill over charcoal or in a grill pan, turning until golden and cooked through.

For the dip, sauté the shallots and garlic in oil, then cook the minced liver through. Add the fermented soybean sauce, water and sugar; simmer until thick. Turn off the heat and stir in the crushed roasted peanuts.
Arrange the grilled pork with rice paper, herbs, green banana, starfruit, cucumber, pickles and crispy rice-paper crackers. Wrap individual portions and dip as you eat.

keywords: Ninh Hoa grilled spring rolls rolled with rice paper

banh-canh-vinh-trung.name: Vinh Trung rice noodle soup
banh-canh-vinh-trung.serving_basis: Four bowls of rice noodle soup with snakehead fish, shrimp, fish cake and clear broth.
banh-canh-vinh-trung.description: Flat rice noodles made from Neáng Nhen rice are chewy and supple, soaked in broth simmered with fish bones and fish, added with snakehead fish, shrimp, fish cakes and rolled pork skin.
banh-canh-vinh-trung.finished_dish: A bowl of Vinh Trung noodle soup with glossy flat rice noodles, clear delicate broth, snakehead fish, shrimp, fish cake and rolled pork skin.
banh-canh-vinh-trung.serving: Serve piping hot, adding the bean sprouts and culantro at the end so they stay crisp and fragrant.
banh-canh-vinh-trung.image_alt: Vinh Trung noodle soup with flat rice noodles, snakehead fish, shrimp, fish cake, rolled pork skin and bean sprouts in a white ceramic bowl.
banh-canh-vinh-trung.time_note: Estimated editorial timing; actual time depends on equipment, ingredients, and cooking experience.
tips: Skim regularly as the broth simmers to keep it clear and gently sweet.
Cook the fish just until done and remove the flesh carefully so it stays in pieces.
Blanch the noodles separately and add the broth just before serving to preserve their springy texture.

ingredients.name: Fresh flat rice bánh canh noodles

preparation_steps: Blanch and rinse the pork and chicken bones. Clean and cut the snakehead fish into pieces; peel and devein the shrimp. Slice the fish cake, rolled pork skin and shallots.
Rinse the bean sprouts, scallions and culantro; finely slice the herbs. If available, use flat noodles made from Neang Nhen rice; otherwise, choose fresh flat rice bánh canh noodles.
cooking_steps: Simmer the pork and chicken bones in water for about 45 minutes, skimming to keep the broth clear. Season to taste with fish sauce, salt and sugar.
Poach the snakehead fish in the broth until just cooked, remove it and gently separate the flesh into pieces. Add the shrimp and cook until just pink, then remove.
Blanch the noodles separately to the desired tenderness and divide among bowls. Arrange the fish, shrimp, fish cake and rolled pork skin on top.
Ladle over the hot broth, then add bean sprouts, scallions, culantro and pepper. Serve at once with lime and chili as desired.

banh-bo-thot-not-kien-giang.name: Kien Giang palm-sugar steamed honeycomb cake
banh-bo-thot-not-kien-giang.serving_basis: About 12 small steamed palm-sugar cakes, served warm or cooled.
banh-bo-thot-not-kien-giang.description: Steamed beef cake fermented from rice flour, coconut milk and palm sugar, has a natural golden brown color, spongy texture and a gentle caramel flavor.
banh-bo-thot-not-kien-giang.finished_dish: Palm-sugar bánh bò has a naturally golden-brown exterior, an airy honeycomb crumb, gentle fermented aroma, mellow coconut richness and a caramel finish.
banh-bo-thot-not-kien-giang.serving: Serve the cakes warm or fully cooled. Sprinkle with fresh grated coconut just before eating.
banh-bo-thot-not-kien-giang.image_alt: Kien Giang palm-sugar bánh bò, naturally golden brown with an airy honeycomb crumb and grated coconut on a ceramic plate.
banh-bo-thot-not-kien-giang.time_note: Estimated editorial timing; actual time depends on equipment, ingredients, and cooking experience.
tips: Palm sugar gives the cakes their colour and caramel aroma; avoid replacing it with coloured syrup.
Let the batter ferment until bubbly and gently fragrant; timing varies with room temperature.
Preheat the moulds for an even rise and do not open the steamer lid too early.
preparation_steps: Grate or finely chop the palm sugar. Bloom the yeast in warm water according to the package directions. Sift the rice flour, tapioca starch and salt into a large bowl.
Warm the coconut milk and stir in the palm sugar until dissolved; let it cool until just warm. Prepare small moulds and brush them lightly with oil.
cooking_steps: Gradually mix the coconut-sugar liquid into the flour, add the bloomed yeast and stir until smooth. Cover and leave in a warm place for 4–6 hours, until bubbles appear and the batter smells gently fermented.

Heat the steamer. Gently stir the fermented batter and fill the preheated moulds about two-thirds full. Steam over high heat for 12–15 minutes, depending on size; keep the lid closed for the first 10 minutes.
Insert a skewer into the centre of a cake; it is done when the skewer comes out clean. Let the cakes cool slightly before unmoulding and serve with grated coconut.

keywords: Kien Giang palm-sugar steamed honeycomb cake
